user_input: My employer in Bangalore has not paid my salary for two months. I have payslips and bank statements.
expected: Cite Payment of Wages Act / Karnataka Shops Act; recommend formal salary demand letter.
actual_response:
[LawPilot AI — Grounded Demo Mode]

### 💼 Employment Legal Analysis: Unpaid Salary & Withheld Dues

**1. Legal Assessment of Your Situation:**
You have reported that your employer has not paid your salary for two months. Under Indian labour law, withholding earned wages for services already rendered is a serious statutory violation.

**2. Applicable Indian Legal Provisions:**
- **[The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 — Section 5 & Section 15](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2405)**: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
- **[The Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 73](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2187)**: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
- **[State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts — Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision](https://shramsuvidha.gov.in/)**: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
- **[The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 — Section 7](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2405)**: Deductions which may be made from wages
- **Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Section 5):** Employers must disburse wages within 7 days (for establishments with < 1,000 employees) or 10 days of the wage period.
- **Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Section 15):** Grants employees the right to file claims for delayed or wrongfully withheld wages before the statutory Authority, along with compensation of up to 10 times the withheld amount.
- **Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Section 73):** Breach of employment terms entitles the employee to full compensation for financial dues owed.

**3. Essential Evidence to Preserve:**
- Appointment letter / employment contract.
- Bank account statements and prior salary slips proving employment and compensation rate.
- Email communications, attendance logs, and WhatsApp messages with management.

**4. Practical Next Steps:**
1. **Send a Formal Demand Notice:** Issue a written 15-day demand notice to the company and HR demanding immediate disbursement.
2. **Approach Labour Authorities:** If unresolved, file a formal complaint before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority under the Payment of Wages Act.

👉 **Next Question for You:** What was your agreed monthly salary and the total unpaid salary amount?

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.
